The production period in marketing history was characterized by a focus on manufacturing efficiency and output, predicated on the assumption that quality, affordable products would sell themselves. This era largely ended as markets became more saturated and competition increased, shifting focus toward sales and marketing techniques. Historically, this transition is generally placed around the 1920s, when the sales era began to take hold after mass production capabilities had been established and consumer demand began to require more persuasion.
